## Overview:
PR #1 updates `SearchController.search` to wrap the API call and result rendering in a `try/catch`, routing failures through `renderError` while preserving the existing abort-and-search flow.

The main risk areas for specialist review are error-contract changes, especially whether aborts and stale requests should be rendered as errors, and whether `renderError` safely accepts every possible rejection value.

## Strengths:
- Preserves the existing active-request cancellation behavior.
- Adds explicit failure handling instead of leaving API rejections unhandled.
- Keeps successful rendering unchanged.

## Minor candidates:
- **[P3] Catch-all handling may surface expected aborts as errors** — **severity:** P3; **why:** every rejection, including cancellation-related failures, now calls `renderError`, which may produce undesirable UI behavior during normal request replacement; **location:** `src/search.ts:24-28`; **side:** head; **in_diff:** yes; **pr_related:** yes; **confidence:** medium.

resolvedReview.overview:
PR #1 updates `SearchController.search` in `src/search.ts` to wrap the API call and result rendering in a `try/catch`, routing failures through `this.renderError(error)` instead of letting rejections propagate. The existing request-supersession flow (`this.active?.abort()` + fresh `AbortController` per call) is unchanged, and the success path behaves identically to before.

This is a reasonable hardening of an otherwise unguarded `await`, but the new catch treats *every* rejection as a renderable error — including the `AbortError` rejections this controller itself produces whenever a newer search supersedes an in-flight one. That leaves one real, non-blocking correctness edge case (below). No blocking defects were found.

findings.title: [P2] Ignore abort errors from superseded searches
findings.body: Every call to `search()` aborts the previous request via `this.active?.abort()` (line 21) and issues a new one with a fresh signal. When the API honors `AbortSignal` (the standard contract implied by passing the signal), the superseded request's promise rejects with an `AbortError`, and the new catch block now calls `this.renderError(error)` for it. Expected cancellation therefore renders as a failure whenever a user triggers a second search before the first completes — flashing an error state that may also overwrite the newer search's UI depending on settlement order. Guard the catch, e.g. return early when `this.active.signal.aborted` or `error.name === 'AbortError'`.

# PR Review

**Verdict:** approve

## Overview

PR #1 updates `SearchController.search` in `src/search.ts` to wrap the API call and result rendering in a `try/catch`, routing failures through `this.renderError(error)` instead of letting rejections propagate. The existing request-supersession flow (`this.active?.abort()` + fresh `AbortController` per call) is unchanged, and the success path behaves identically to before.

This is a reasonable hardening of an otherwise unguarded `await`, but the new catch treats *every* rejection as a renderable error — including the `AbortError` rejections this controller itself produces whenever a newer search supersedes an in-flight one. That leaves one real, non-blocking correctness edge case (below). No blocking defects were found.

## Verification

Verification did not run: it is disabled because no user-level `verificationBaselines` profiles are configured (`pr_review_verify` list returned `enabled: false`, no baselines). Disclosure: baseline execution would run PR code unsandboxed (filesystem/network) with lifecycle supervision limited to the original POSIX process group; use an external sandbox or container wrapper for untrusted PRs.

## Findings

### [P2] Ignore abort errors from superseded searches
**Severity:** P2
**Rationale:** Every call to `search()` aborts the previous request via `this.active?.abort()` (line 21) and issues a new one with a fresh signal. When the API honors `AbortSignal` (the standard contract implied by passing the signal), the superseded request's promise rejects with an `AbortError`, and the new catch block now calls `this.renderError(error)` for it. Expected cancellation therefore renders as a failure whenever a user triggers a second search before the first completes — flashing an error state that may also overwrite the newer search's UI depending on settlement order. Guard the catch, e.g. return early when `this.active.signal.aborted` or `error.name === 'AbortError'`.
**Location:** `src/search.ts:26-27 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness

All requested lanes completed.

## Strengths and notes

- Preserves the existing cancel-on-new-search behavior and keeps the success path (`render`) unchanged.
- Adds explicit failure handling instead of leaving API rejections unhandled.

Correctness: one P2 edge case above; otherwise logic is sound. Security: no concerns in the changed lines. Performance: no regressions.

Notes: `search()` previously returned a rejected promise on API failure and now resolves after rendering the error. No callers of `search()` exist in the repository to be affected, and routing errors to `renderError` looks intentional — but if external consumers rely on the rejection, consider rethrowing after rendering.
